title: Abba bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: An Amora mentioned once in the Babylonian Talmud and once in the Jerusalem Talmud; Hyman states that, in truth, no such Amora existed. Eruvin 63a mentions R’ Abba bar Tachlifa together with R-A of Hagronya [ר״א מהגרוניא]; Hyman says it should read R’ Acha bar Tachlifa, as later in the same discussion and in Dikdukei Soferim. Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni [supplied פ״ס ה״ז; digital comparison 4:4] has ‘Chiyya bar Bun, Abba bar Tachlifa, in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya’; Hyman says it should read Ada bar Tachlifa, as later in the same account. Regarding Eruvin 40a, ‘Rava bar Tachlifa said to Ravina,’ Hyman says, ‘We have already explained that it was written רב״א, and it is Rav Acha bar Tachlifa.’ Regarding Rabbah or Rava bar Tachlifa in Shabbat 102b and Chullin 45b and 49a, he says, ‘We have already explained in his entry that he was a student of Rav, and this is clear.’

notes.text: The checked Eruvin explicitly names Rabbi Elazar of Hagronya and alternates Abba/Acha bar Tachlifa. The supplied Maaser Sheni chapter label פ״ס remains corrupt; chapter 5 is not silently substituted.

Hyman’s once-in-each-Talmud and in-truth-no-such-Amora assertions, both definite SHOULD READ corrections, his earlier Rav-A explanation, and his this-is-clear conclusion retain their force as his argument, not an admitted historical nonexistence or authority merger. The uninspected Eruvin comparison is inherited only; Abba/Acha titles remain R-prime, and ambiguous ר״א מהגרוניא is left literal R-A rather than selecting Elazar or Eliezer from an uninspected prior report. The whole saved Mechon-Mamre Maaser Sheni 4:4 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Hoshaya in the quoted chain, supporting that full title locally. It has untitled Chiyya bar Bun and Abba bar Tachlifa juxtaposed without an added conjunction or invented reporting links. The digital match is shown beside supplied פ״ס ה״ז, not a proven repair to that label. The search’s claimed second occurrence is not separately bound here. Hyman’s Ada correction is not established by this Abba reading. The supplied same-discussion form באותו שנין and other irregular spellings stay in Hebrew; the English same-discussion reading is contextual. Two occurrences of we have already explained are Hyman’s first-person plural; Ravina/Rabbah/Rava remain names without added titles, and full Rav remains for explicit Acha and the final teacher Rav. All source holds remain.

The consulted Eruvin 63a names Elazar of Hagronya and has Abba bar Tachlifa followed by Acha bar Tachlifa. Dikdukei Soferim (Eruvin, p. 252, note ל) places printed Abba beside manuscript Acha in the first occurrence. At Jerusalem Maaser Sheni 4:4, the consulted Mechon Mamre text names Abba and Rabbi Hoshaya. The consulted Guggenheimer text names Ada and Rav Hoshaya. These are comparisons with the supplied locator and Hyman’s emendation. The consulted Eruvin 40a has Rava address Ravina, while Hyman proposes Acha. His assertion that there was no such Amora is his conclusion from these readings.
